correctness.rationale: An explicit matrix computation proves the three-minor commutation criterion without characteristic assumptions. For each ideal valuation s the primitive quotient triple has a unique projective direction and unit-scalar fiber; projective reduction has q^2 children per node. Vanishing minors for two vectors is equivalent either to s+t >= ell or coincidence of projective ancestors at level ell-s-t. These facts construct a universal graph isomorphism for equal parameters. Independent counting gives exactly ell+1 degree values and q^(4 ell) vertices, recovering ell and q. Four fully enumerated finite test pairs and an independent 65,536-pair direct matrix census confirm the formulas; finite checks are not substituted for the argument.

The new if-and-only-if cross-ring classification applies to arbitrary chain rings of the same q and ell and has a concrete nonisomorphic pair of matrix rings. value.rationale: A complete natural iff classification of 2x2 matrix-ring commuting graphs over all finite commutative chain rings recovers the only surviving parameters (q, ell), and the exact centralizer-degree census follows. The explicit isomorphism between graphs of M_2(Z/4) and M_2(F_2[t]/t^2), matrix rings of different additive exponent, exhibits a structural limit of graph reconstruction. The effect is not a narrow numerical increment: it applies uniformly in all residue prime powers and nilpotency lengths.
